visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Unlevered FCF is 50, interest is 20, the tax rate is 25% and no debt is repaid. What's levered FCF?
questions.explain: Interest cuts the tax bill: 20 of interest saves 5 of tax, so it costs 15. 50 − 15 = 35. Taking off the full 20 gives 30.
questions.explain_at: Twenty of interest, five of it back through tax

questions.q: What discount rate do you use for levered free cash flow, and what value does it give you?

options.text: Cost of debt, giving equity value
Cost of equity, giving equity value

questions.explain: Levered FCF belongs only to shareholders, so it's discounted at what shareholders demand, the cost of equity, and gives equity value. WACC goes with unlevered FCF and enterprise value.
questions.explain_at: so you discount it at the cost of equity

questions.q: Your levered DCF gives 600m. Net debt is 200m. What equity value do you report?
questions.explain: Interest and repayments are already inside levered cash flows, so the result is equity value. Subtracting net debt again charges shareholders for the debt twice.
questions.explain_at: Subtract net debt again, and you've charged shareholders for the debt twice

questions.q: Why do bankers usually prefer an unlevered DCF in mergers and acquisitions?

options.text: It's simpler, with no debt to model
It gives a higher value than levered
Value doesn't depend on the funding
It captures the target's current debt

questions.explain: A buyer will choose its own financing, so you want the value of the business itself, whatever it's funded with. Simplicity is a side benefit, not the main reason.
questions.explain_at: In a deal, the buyer will choose its own financing

questions.q: Informa is paying an enterprise value of about £2.24bn for Clarion. Which DCF do you compare that price with?

options.text: Levered: Informa is raising money to pay
Unlevered: the price is an enterprise value
Levered, at the weighted average cost

questions.explain: An enterprise value is the price of the whole business, so it's compared with unlevered cash flows discounted at the WACC. The target's old debt and the buyer's funding don't change what the business is worth.
questions.explain_at: The price is an enterprise value, the whole business
